name: A cost on interaction magnitude prunes correlations not shared by all selected targets
precondition: The selective targets are drawn from a class built by combining independent modules, so some trait-trait correlations are present in every target (structural) and others only in the sampled subset (incidental). The map's parameters must evolve slower than the traits they control.
mechanism: Fitness carries a penalty proportional to sum|b_ij| (L1) or sum b_ij^2 (L2). Interactions that pay their cost only on a subset of the selected targets are removed or shrunk; interactions that pay on every selected target are retained.
immediate_effect: The evolved interaction matrix converges towards the block-diagonal variance-covariance structure of the whole class rather than of the sampled subset.
future_variation_effect: The distribution of phenotypes the map produces from arbitrary embryonic states concentrates on the module-combinatorial family. Under L1 the entropy of that distribution converges to EXACTLY the number of modules in bits (4), meaning the modules vary independently.
acquisition_effect: Under a frozen map, hill-climbing reaches unselected members of the class faster, and under L1 reaches at least one member that is unreachable under the control map. Both ACQUIRES_FASTER and REACHES_PREVIOUSLY_UNREACHABLE are observed.
intervention_evidence: Four arms (control, noise, L2, L1) with the detector run in all four (Fig 3) and the acquisition assay run in all four (Fig 5). NOT causally identified: the intervention acts on fitness, both readouts are functionals of the resulting map, and no arm holds accessibility fixed. No replication is reported for the longitudinal arms.
substrate_dependence: HIGH. Depends on the target class being generated by independent modules, on the two-timescale separation between B and G, and on the cost acting on the same parameters that carry the correlations. The exhaustive training-set analysis shows the effect is small or absent for training sets of 1-2 patterns, so it also depends on having enough examples.
confounds_to_carry: A cost on interaction magnitude also reduces expressible variety outright. Under-fitting at high lambda is reported by the authors, so the mechanism has a two-sided failure mode and the 'right' pressure is tuned, not derived.

name: Noise on the selective target slows but does not prevent canalisation
precondition: As above, plus a noise scale small enough not to destroy the selection signal.
mechanism: Gaussian noise added to the target vector every generation, scaled by kappa.
immediate_effect: Regulatory coefficients evolve to smaller magnitudes; relative ordering of strong and weak correlations is preserved.
future_variation_effect: Test error reaches a minimum (0.34) and then degrades; the map spends longer in a well-generalising state.
acquisition_effect: Faster adaptation than control; some class members remain unreachable.
intervention_evidence: One arm, detector and acquisition both measured. Same identification limits as above.
substrate_dependence: Kappa must be tuned; the authors report an optimum at 35e-4 and degradation on both sides.
confounds_to_carry: The authors are explicit that noise only POSTPONES over-fitting rather than preventing it, so this is a rate effect, not a structural one.

name: Selection for immediate fitness necessarily enlarges the developmental basin of the selected phenotype
source_note: From the sibling Kounios et al. 2016 (arXiv 1612.05955), not from the specimen.
precondition: A recurrent developmental map whose interactions can be adjusted while the embryonic state is held at a selected phenotype.
mechanism: Regulatory changes that raise the fitness of the currently expressed phenotype reinforce the correlations present in that phenotype, which enlarges the set of embryonic states that develop into it.
future_variation_effect: The number of G vectors mapping to that phenotype rises over evolutionary time, measured directly as the basin of attraction (Fig 8). The authors call this a 'systematic side-effect' of short-term selection.
acquisition_effect: Over deep time the map lets microevolution reach higher-fitness phenotypes from arbitrary starting points, verified against a one-to-one-map null over 30 replicates with Mann-Whitney U tests.
intervention_evidence: A genuine representational on/off ablation (one-to-one map vs evolving GRN) with the mutation operator held identical. STILL NOT the composition: the basin detector is measured in one unablated condition only, and in the ablated arms the longitudinal quantity is the outcome itself.
substrate_dependence: Requires the recurrent attractor dynamics; would not transfer to a feed-forward or one-to-one map by construction.
confounds_to_carry: Enlarging a basin is increased ROBUSTNESS, which by itself OPPOSES evolvability. The authors say so directly. The evolvability claim depends on what happens to OTHER basins when the map evolves slowly across many peaks, not on this mechanism alone.
